data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

Section 11101 et seq.; E- Government Act of 2002, 44 U.S.C. § 3501; The Common Approach to Federal Enterprise Architecture (“Common Approach”); Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837; Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA 2014), 44 U.S.C. § 3551; and various Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance documents.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy and approach to Enterprise Architecture (EA) in support of the Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 11101 et seq.; E- Government Act of 2002, 44 U.S.C. § 3501; The Common Approach to Federal Enterprise Architecture (“Common Approach”); Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837; Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA 2014), 44 U.S.C. § 3551; and various Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance documents.
cross_references: Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 11101 et seq.
The Common Approach to Federal Enterprise Architecture (“Common Approach”)
Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837
Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA 2014), 44 U.S.C. § 3551
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy and approach to Enterprise Architecture (EA)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of information technology (IT) and Enterprise Architecture.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA
conditions: who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of information technology (IT) and Enterprise Architecture

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3185-001, Enterprise Architecture, dated July 29, 2019.
This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded or expiration.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: EA procedures will be provided in the companion Departmental Manual(DM) 3185-001, Enterprise Architecture Procedures.

FITARA requires Chief Information Officers (CIO) to have a significant role in Information Technology (IT) decisions,including annual and multi-year planning, programming, budgeting, execution, reporting, management, governance, and oversight functions.

USDA’s EA is an asset that captures and contextualizes information and data regarding the Department’s and its Mission Area, agency, and staff office business operations, capabilities, and supporting technologies.
EA supports and provides information for USDA’s IT investment and management processes and seeks to reduce unnecessary duplication of both material expenditures and efforts.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s IT investment and management processes

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects must comply with legislative mandates, Federal initiatives, and oversight requirements, which includes the Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework Version 2 (FEAF v2) taxonomy and the Technology Business Management Council, Technology Business Management Taxonomy.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: legislative mandates, Federal initiatives, and oversight requirements
cross_references: Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework Version 2 (FEAF v2)
Technology Business Management Council, Technology Business Management Taxonomy

policy_statements.source_text: USDA’s Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects will:
Align with and support the business and operational needs, requirements, and priorities expressed through the USDA Strategic Plan Fiscal Years 2022-2026;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: business and operational needs, requirements, and priorities expressed through the USDA Strategic Plan Fiscal Years 2022-2026

policy_statements.source_text: Conform to the USDA Standards Profile as approved by the Enterprise Architecture Committee (EAC).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
conditions: as approved by the Enterprise Architecture Committee (EAC)

policy_statements.source_text: Usage of unapproved standards may occur if the responsible Mission Area, agency, or staff office has received an exception via theUSDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Acquisition Approval Request process;
conditions: if the responsible Mission Area, agency, or staff office has received an exception via theUSDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Acquisition Approval Request process

policy_statements.source_text: Incorporate security controls for all systems and applications to ensure the authorization, integrity, completeness, and accuracy of transactions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: security controls for all systems and applications

policy_statements.source_text: Be designed and implemented in the context of the USDA EA and carried out to create a more responsive and cost-effective Government;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
conditions: in the context of the USDA EA

policy_statements.source_text: Install a robust configuration management process that must be in place for systems, applications, and data;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure data is an asset that has value to the enterprise and is managed accordingly;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects

policy_statements.source_text: Utilize the Enterprise Architecture Visioning Environment (EAVE) to develop and maintain the Mission Area, agency, and staff office IT asset inventory and their attributes;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office IT asset inventory and their attributes

policy_statements.source_text: Identify legacy systems which include IT assets with an expected decommission date of less than 5 years;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
conditions: which include IT assets with an expected decommission date of less than 5 years

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain legacy system classifications within EAVE (e.g., expected decommission dates, actual decommission dates and an expected decommission reason) for all applicable IT assets within the Mission Area, agency, and staff office inventory;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
conditions: for all applicable IT assets within the Mission Area, agency, and staff office inventory

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and maintain the Mission Area, agency, and staff office application roadmap or strategy to support strategic goals and technology modernization efforts, to include modernizing legacy systems by re-architecting, rebuilding, or replacing; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office application roadmap or strategy

policy_statements.source_text: Provide the OCIO, Information Resource Management Center (IRMC), Enterprise Architecture Division (EAD) with the most current Mission Area, agency, and staff office application roadmap or strategy for inclusion into the USDA OCIO Target Architecture to facilitate effective decision-making.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Enterprise Architects
policy_statements.target: OCIO, Information Resource Management Center (IRMC), Enterprise Architecture Division (EAD)

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Appoint a Chief Enterprise Architect (CEA) for USDA;
Provide sufficient support to ensure the USDA’s EA is effectively and efficiently governed;
Ensure that the EA program complies with applicable laws, OMB policies and memorandum, USDA policies and procedures, and has an effective governance process; and

Ensure that EA practices, principles, and information are incorporated into IT governance, portfolio management, capital planning, investment management, and other processes related to the planning, acquisition, maintenance, end of life and disposition of IT.
policy_statements.target: IT governance, portfolio management, capital planning, investment management, and other processes related to the planning, acquisition, maintenance, end of life and disposition of IT

policy_statements.source_text: The IRMC Associate Chief Information Officer will:
Address USDA’s information and IT requirements as collaborative and integrated processes, and work in concert with the USDA EAC;
Implement, manage, monitor, maintain, and report on USDA’s infrastructure and office automation technology base (i.e., its shared services environment); and
policy_statements.target: USDA’s infrastructure and office automation technology base (i.e., its shared services environment)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure tight integration of USDA’s EA, Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC), program management, and IT waiver processes.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s EA, Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC), program management, and IT waiver processes

policy_statements.source_text: USDA OCIO CEA will:
Disseminate and make available the contents of the USDA’s EA program;
policy_statements.target: contents of the USDA’s EA program

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC) Chair and direct and oversee all meetings;
policy_statements.target: Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the Chair and oversee and establish EAC Integrated Project Teams to address specific processes, work, or issues;
Provide day-to-day management and stewardship of USDA’s EAD;
Conduct periodic reviews of Mission Area, agency, and staff office EA activities;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office EA activities

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate USDA’s EA-specific responses to internal and external oversight organizations (Government Accountability Office, General Services Administration, OMB, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and other organizations or Federal agencies);
policy_statements.target: internal and external oversight organizations (Government Accountability Office, General Services Administration, OMB, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and other organizations or Federal agencies)

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee an Enterprise Architecture Repository (EAR) that supports enterprise IT decision making and reporting activities;
Align USDA Classifications and Standards with OMB EA Standards for compliance.
This can be integrated with the USDA EAR; and
Ensure creation and dissemination of a detailed operating procedures, policies, and other core EA artifacts that define the operation of the EAD.
policy_statements.target: detailed operating procedures, policies, and other core EA artifacts that define the operation of the EAD

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC) will:
Be chaired by the USDA CEA;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)

policy_statements.source_text: Be comprised of three to five voting members from the USDA CIO Council;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)

policy_statements.source_text: Provide overall strategic direction and guidance for USDA’s EA;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the Department’s senior governing body for EA and be primarily responsible for facilitating the development and prioritization of EA strategies;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as an adjudicating authority for the resolution of any issues that arise from or are identified by the EAC;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)
conditions: that arise from or are identified by the EAC

policy_statements.source_text: Assist in the establishment of a shared understanding of current EA challenges within the USDA and potential solutions for overcoming them; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)
policy_statements.target: shared understanding of current EA challenges within the USDA and potential solutions for overcoming them

policy_statements.source_text: Facilitate agreement on a future-state vision for the USDA’s EA.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Enterprise Architecture Executive Steering Committee (EA ESC)
policy_statements.target: future-state vision for the USDA’s EA

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA EAC will:
Be chaired by the USDA CEA;
Be comprised of one voting member from each agency and staff office;
Collaborate with Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices in the creation, maintenance, and updating of EA-related standards, guidelines, directives, policies and procedures within USDA;
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Establish EA value and performance measures;
Assess compliance with, completeness of, and benefits derived directly and indirectly from the use of the USDA EA; and
Develop and maintain EA reference models and make recommendations to the EA ESC and the USDA’s CIO Council for improvements to USDA’s EA domains.
policy_statements.target: EA ESC and the USDA’s CIO Council

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CIOs will:
Ensure collaboration and coordination of EA functions across agency and Mission Area leadership, Enterprise Architects, and the USDA CEA;
policy_statements.target: agency and Mission Area leadership, Enterprise Architects, and the USDA CEA

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint and oversee data content stewards to ensure the accuracy and timeliness of data content in the USDA;
Align each IT project with USDA’s EA vision, principles, and standards; is consistent with agreements reached through collaborative decision-making processes; and is represented in the EAR; and
Develop internal policies, procedures, and controls to support the EA function.
Agency and Staff Office IT Directors and Program Managers will:
Incorporate EA policies, requirements, and standards into agency and staff office IT governance and CPIC processes;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and Staff Office IT Directors and Program Managers
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office IT governance and CPIC processes

policy_statements.source_text: Implement and maintain business, performance, application, data, infrastructure,and security configuration settings and controls;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and Staff Office IT Directors and Program Managers
policy_statements.target: business, performance, application, data, infrastructure,and security configuration settings and controls

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Enterprise Architects and decision makers share a consistent understanding of the unique requirements for each EA subject area; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and Staff Office IT Directors and Program Managers

policy_statements.source_text: Stay current on trends, developments, and innovations pertaining to EA-related tools, methods, and frameworks in the public and private sectors.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and Staff Office IT Directors and Program Managers
policy_statements.target: trends, developments, and innovations pertaining to EA-related tools, methods, and frameworks in the public and private sectors

policy_statements.source_text: All inquiries regarding this DR will be directed to the USDA OCIO IRMC EAD at enterprise.architecture@ocio.usda.gov.

citation.matching_text: Office of the Chief Information Officer, Information Resources Management Center

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy and approach to Enterprise Architecture (EA) in support of the *Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996*,  40 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 11101 *et seq.* ; *E- Government Act of 2002*,  44 U.S.C. § 3501 ;  *The Common Approach to Federal Enterprise Architecture*  (“*Common Approach*”); *Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act* (FITARA),  Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837 ; *Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014* (FISMA 2014),  44 U.S.C. § 3551 ; and various Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance documents.

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of information technology (IT) and Enterprise Architecture.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy and approach to Enterprise Architecture (EA) in support of the *Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996*,  40 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 11101 *et seq.* ; *E- Government Act of 2002*,  44 U.S.C. § 3501 ;  *The Common Approach to Federal Enterprise Architecture*  (“*Common Approach*”); *Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act* (FITARA),  Public Law (P.L.) 113-291 § 831-837 ; *Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014* (FISMA 2014),  44 U.S.C. § 3551 ; and various Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance documents.
United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy and approach to Enterprise Architecture (EA)

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of information technology (IT) and Enterprise Architecture.

FITARA requires Chief Information Officers (CIO) to have a significant role in Information Technology (IT) decisions,including annual and multi-year planning, programming, budgeting, execution, reporting, management, governance, and oversight functions.

USDA’s EA is an asset that captures and contextualizes information and data regarding the Department’s and its Mission Area, agency, and staff office business operations, capabilities, and supporting technologies.
EA supports and provides information for USDA’s IT investment and management processes and seeks to reduce unnecessary duplication of both material expenditures and efforts.
